title: Find K Closest Elements
spaceBreakdown:
- returned vector<int> of size k: not counted (output)
- lo, hi, mid, n: O(1) scalars
- no recursion, no auxiliary containers
approach: Since the array is sorted and ties favor smaller values, the k closest elements always form a contiguous subarray of length k. Binary search for the optimal left boundary: for a candidate left index `mid`, compare `arr[mid]` against `arr[mid+k]` - if `x - arr[mid] > arr[mid+k] - x`, the right element is closer (or equally close but larger), so shift the window right; otherwise keep it. This narrows to the best starting index in O(log(n−k)), then we slice k elements.
hints: Given the array is sorted and ties prefer smaller values, what can you say about the positions of the k chosen elements relative to each other in the array? The array length is at most 10^4.

Binary search on the left index of a contiguous size-k window. For arr=[1,2,3,4,5], k=4, x=3: compare arr[0]=1 and arr[4]=5 - both distance 2 from 3, so keep the left boundary; window starts at index 0.

**Ties** - equal distance on both sides, smaller value must win
`Input: arr = [1,2,3,4,5], k = 4, x = 3` → `Expected: [1,2,3,4]`
⚠️ Bug: using `>=` instead of `>` in the comparison → shifts right on tie, returns `[2,3,4,5]`

**Single element** - n = 1, the window has no room to move
`Input: arr = [7], k = 1, x = 3` → `Expected: [7]`
⚠️ Bug: initializing `hi = n` instead of `n - k` → accesses `arr[0 + 1]` out of bounds

**Duplicates** - repeated values create multi-way ties that test preference for the leftmost block
`Input: arr = [1,1,1,2,2,3], k = 3, x = 2` → `Expected: [1,2,2]`
⚠️ Bug: using `>=` instead of `>` → returns `[2,2,3]`

**x far above all elements** - every distance is negative on the array side, sign of the comparison matters
`Input: arr = [1,2,3,4,5], k = 3, x = 100` → `Expected: [3,4,5]`
⚠️ Bug: comparing `arr[mid] - x > arr[mid+k] - x` (wrong sign) → returns `[1,2,3]`

followUps.q: What if arr is an unbounded stream and you must maintain the k closest to x at all times?
followUps.a: Keep a max-heap of size k keyed by (|v−x|, −v); when size exceeds k, evict the worst element. Each insertion costs O(log k), total O(n log k) time and O(k) space. Flush and sort the heap contents when queried.

followUps.q: What if you receive many (x, k) queries on the same fixed sorted array?
followUps.a: Each query runs the same binary search independently in O(log n + k). No preprocessing helps asymptotically because the comparison depends on x, so total cost is O(q(log n + k)) for q queries.

followUps.q: What if the array is not sorted?
followUps.a: Binary search no longer applies. Use a max-heap of size k keyed by (|arr[i]−x|, −arr[i]) in O(n log k) time, then sort the k survivors. Alternatively, quickselect the k-th closest in O(n) average and sort those k elements.
